ink.purpose: The object itself. Opaque, never translucent — glass reads as another app's chrome.

paper.purpose: The single committed action on screen. Its scarcity is what makes it read as the commitment.

live.purpose: Armed state and the 2px focus ring. Encodes readiness, nothing decorative.

redline.purpose: Removal, and only removal. A mark staged for deletion, never a warning or an error.

working.purpose: The running loader. The one colour that means the agent has the batch.

halo.purpose: The outer half of every on-page outline, so a mark reads on white, black or a photograph.

indicator.purpose: A small solid mark at rest: the status dot, the consequence bullet, the comment box thumb.

yellow.purpose: The wordmark's own colour, from the source file. Two places on the landing page and nowhere else.

display.purpose: The full-page notice the CLI serves when the proxied dev server cannot be reached. Never inside the island.

label.purpose: Actions and titles in the island.

strong.purpose: The committed action, and a row's kind.

count.purpose: The staged count on the pill. Tabular.

address.purpose: Source file and line. The only monospace, so paths align down the batch list.

wordmark.purpose: The mark in the landing page masthead, at the source file's own metrics.

wordmark-footer.purpose: The same mark in the footer, never enlarged into a poster.

page-lede.purpose: The hero paragraph under the headline.

page-body-large.purpose: The upper bound of fluid showcase copy.

page-kbd.purpose: Gesture key chips on the landing page.

shadows.name: island
shadows.purpose: The island at rest and expanded. One soft cast plus a hairline inner light, so the object holds an edge against a white host and a black one.

shadows.name: near
shadows.purpose: Chrome sitting directly on the page — the composer and the text bar — which is nearer the reader than the island.

shadows.name: on-element
shadows.purpose: The version and slider pills, which perch on the element rather than float over the page.

shadows.name: ring-halo
shadows.purpose: Every on-page outline. The pair is what survives an unknown background; a single stroke does not.

shadows.name: ring-halo-remove
shadows.purpose: The same pair for a removal, thicker because redline on a busy page needs the weight.

shadows.name: badge-halo
shadows.purpose: The reference badge, which is small enough that it needs a lighter halo than the ring it sits on.

motion.name: morph
motion.purpose: Every shape change. Width and height together, 140ms for a small adjustment up to 380ms for a full open.

motion.name: settle
motion.purpose: 460ms, for the island travelling to a corner. Longer and softer than the morph, because it is travel rather than a change of shape.

motion.name: cross-fade
motion.purpose: Content inside a morphing container. Always starts after the shape has begun moving.

motion.name: mark-land
motion.purpose: A mark arriving on the page. Marks never fade in.

motion.name: arm
motion.purpose: The armed state in and out, because it has to feel instantaneous.

components.name: Island — batch pill
components.description: The resting object: staged count and the action. Its label is the state; the action never moves, because the row packs against the anchored corner.

components.name: Review row
components.description: One staged mark in the panel: number, kind, flags, address, comment, drop. The flags are their own column. The dimmed variant is a mark whose element is no longer on screen — hollow number, never red.

narrative.northStar: One small dark object at the corner of someone else's app, which changes shape to match its state.
narrative.overview:
Not a toolbar, not a panel system, not a set of windows that open and close. A single continuous thing that is tiny when there is nothing to say and grows only as far as the current state requires. Everything Tailr needs to tell you happens by that object changing shape.

Motion is the identity here, and it is the one place Tailr spends. The island morphs; it does not appear. Shape changes animate width and height together, longer than product-UI convention, because the morph is the thing being expressed — and every one of them is interruptible, because two animations on the same pill is what makes rapid hovering flicker.

Tailr renders inside applications it does not own, so restraint is structural rather than stylistic: no translucency, no glass, no second bar, and no colour that does not encode state. What it draws on the host page is drawn as a halo pair, because a single stroke does not survive an unknown background.
keyCharacteristics: One object, many shapes — states are transitions of the same element, never new elements appearing.
Resting size is the design; every pixel it occupies at rest must be earned.
The page is never touched: no dimming, tinting, insetting, padding, resizing or restyling of the host.
One radius in every state (19px), so collapsed it is a pill and expanded it is a window — never a different object.
Exactly one paper element on screen; its scarcity is what makes it read as the commitment.
Colour is state-encoding only: live for armed, redline for removal, working for the agent.

rules.name: The One Object Rule
rules.body: States are transitions of the same element, never new elements appearing. If something new must be shown, the island morphs to contain it.

rules.name: The Resting Size Rule
rules.body: Idle is nearly nothing. Every pixel it occupies at rest must be earned.

rules.name: The Untouched Page Rule
rules.body: No dimming, tinting, insetting, padding, resizing, or restyling of the host application.

rules.name: The One Radius Rule
rules.body: The island carries one radius in every state — 19px, exactly half its 38px resting height — with no radius transition between them. A panel that changes its corner as it grows announces itself as a different object.

rules.name: The Halo Pair Rule
rules.body: Every on-page outline is a paired stroke: ink inside, halo outside. Test on white, on black, and on a photograph.

rules.name: The Pointer-Alone Rule
rules.body: The version pill's width must follow the pointer alone. Expanding on a class the pointer has just caused feeds the geometry back into the hover that produced it, and the page flickers between versions while the pointer sits still.

rules.name: The Row Follows Its Mark Rule
rules.body: Reopening a mark changes neither the length of the list nor any status in it, so a panel that redraws on those alone goes on showing the note the composer over it has already replaced.

rules.name: The Nothing Is Red Rule
rules.body: A hidden mark is dimmed rather than coloured. Nothing in that state is red, because nothing in it has gone wrong — the element stopped rendering, and the mark is intact.

rules.name: The Told And Not Told Rule
rules.body: The reviewer is told a mark is hidden and the agent is not: the missing badge is the reviewer's to explain, and the batch has nothing to say about it.

rules.name: The Live Indicator Rule
rules.body: A running indicator is never re-created by a re-render. Rewriting the node restarts its animation, and a spinner that restarts every time a result lands reads as stalling rather than working.

dos: Make idle nearly invisible, then let hover do the work.
Animate the container and its content as one gesture.
Keep exactly one `paper` element on screen.

Suppress the platform's scrollbar on every engine, not just the one in front of you — a strip of the host browser's chrome is a seam across an object Tailr drew every other pixel of. Where scrolling then needs to be legible, draw the bar: the staged list scrolls bare, and the comment box carries a 4px `indicator` thumb on a transparent track, present only while there is somewhere to scroll.
Draw every on-page mark as a halo pair; test on white, on black, and on a photograph.
donts: Never dim, tint, inset, pad, resize, or restyle the host page.
No translucency, no backdrop blur, no glass.
No leader lines, no callout balloons, no technical-drawing apparatus. The reference number is a small corner badge and nothing more.
No second bar, dock, sidebar, or persistent panel. If it can't be the island, it doesn't ship.
No color that doesn't encode state.
